title: The cloud-wave budget test fails intermittently under CI load
description:
FOUND 2026-09-23 on PR #38's CI: run-workflow.test.ts > 'a cloud wave in flight answers to a stop and to a budget > stops dispatching further batches once the cost budget is spent' FAILED on the CI runner. The same commit's re-run passed; main's CI on the same code passed; the whole file passed 88/88 three times locally. #38 changed only .github/workflows/ci.yml.

So it is load- or timing-dependent - the same class as owf (the epic-reconciler lease-lapse test). Per the flaky-means-bug rule it is a defect: a test that samples a condition it should wait for, or races wall time. Reproduce it deterministically (under CPU contention or with the fake clock pinned) before changing anything; do not raise a timeout to make it pass.
notes: 2026-09-23 11:44 - ESCALATED 2026-09-23, and now P1: this flake class is BLOCKING EPIC CLOSE-OUTS, not just colouring PRs. wne's close-out stopped twice on CI red; the second time six tests in one block all hit their 15s timeout together on the CI runner (run 35837696840: 'shows a cloud run live, with per-tick state and substrate-shaped sources', 'reports the durable verdict...', 'carries the gateway's cost on the closing event...', 'publishes no cost at all when the gateway telemetry could not be read', 'completes and collects identically when every event is dropped', 'streams the Phase 1 single-orchestrator run too...'), while a second CI run on the same head passed. Two aggravators: close-out requires EVERY check green, and since #38 each epic head gets TWO CI runs (push + pull_request), doubling the exposure. These tests wait on wall time with fixed deadlines against a simulated Workflow engine, so a slow runner fails them. Same class as owf. Belongs with t8u (deterministic contention).
acceptance_criteria: The failure is reproduced deterministically and its cause named; the test no longer depends on wall time or scheduling under load; the file passes repeatedly under induced CPU contention
